newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close down on institutional sales.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close down on institutional sales.

text.p: Singapore shares closed weaker on Thursday as institutional selling and a revision of a key index stock sent the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) down sharply.
"A lot of institutional funds are trying to sell and move up into north Asia markets," one local dealer said.
"The Keppel bonus issue hit us," said another of the STII's revision to account for Keppel Corp's one-for-four bonus issue.
The STII hit a low of 2,000.44 in early trade, but recovered to end off 14.63 at 2,020.17.
"We're trading in a range of 1,950 to 2,050 and we'll be there for at least the next two to three months," a dealer said.
Keppel led 284 losers, down Singapore $1.85 to S$6.80.
The foreign tranches of UOB, DBS and OCBC bank stocks all tumbled S$0.50 on concerns about new mortgage lending rules and worries over potential exposure to Thailand's financial crisis.
Singapore Telecom shares fell eight cents to S$2.54, after recovering from an all-time low of S$2.50.
Creative Technology led 71 gainers, up S$0.70 at S$20.30.
Total market volume was 111.8 million shares.
